items.prompt: Count the 1 bits of a 32-bit integer, in time proportional to the number of 1 bits.
items.why: n & (n − 1) clears the lowest set bit, so the loop runs once per set bit (Kernighan).

items.prompt: Every number in the array appears twice except one. Find it in O(1) space.
items.why: Pairs cancel under XOR (a ^ a = 0), so one running XOR leaves the single number. That's the Bitwise XOR pattern.

items.prompt: Every number appears three times except one. Find it in O(1) extra space.
items.why: Triples don't cancel under XOR. Count each bit position across all numbers, mod 3, and rebuild the single value (watch the sign bit).

items.prompt: Decide in O(1) whether a positive integer is a power of two.
items.why: A power of two has exactly one set bit, so n > 0 and n & (n − 1) == 0. Repeated division would be O(log n).

items.prompt: Return all subsets of a list of distinct integers.
items.why: Producing every subset is the Subsets pattern (build level by level). Looping masks 0..2ⁿ−1 is just another way to write it.

items.prompt: Visit all of 15 cities exactly once with minimum total distance.
items.why: Overlapping subproblems over (visited set, last city) → bitmask DP in O(2ⁿ · n²). The mask is only the state encoding.

items.prompt: Given up to 1000 lowercase words, find the maximum product of the lengths of two words that share no letter.
items.why: Each word's letter set fits in a 26-bit mask, so the 'disjoint?' test per pair is a single AND.

items.prompt: Add two 32-bit integers without using + or −.
items.why: a ^ b is the sum without carries and (a & b) << 1 is the carry. Loop until the carry is 0, masking to 32 bits.
